issues.description: The solution's Person class declares the first-name field as 'forename' but all getters, setters, and equals/hashCode reference 'firstName'. This name mismatch inside src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java in the solution repository is a structural defect that will cause compilation errors and prevents students from using the provided solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field name consistent with the rest of the class. Either rename the declared field 'forename' to 'firstName' in src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java (recommended to match template and existing getters/setters), or update all getters/setters/equals/hashCode to use 'forename'. Ensure the field name matches across declaration, accessors, and equals/hashCode so the class compiles and behaves as intended.

issues.description: The Person model's first-name attribute is inconsistently named between template and solution. In the template the field is declared as 'firstName', but in the solution the field was renamed to 'forename' while the getters, setters, equals(), and hashCode() in the solution still reference 'firstName'. This mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping for students (they expect a 'firstName' property) and results in inconsistent/incorrect code in the solution (references to a non-existent field).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent identifier for the first-name attribute across all artifacts. Recommended: rename the solution field back to 'firstName' (private String firstName;) and ensure getters/setters, equals(), and hashCode() reference 'firstName'. Alternatively, if 'forename' is preferred, update all getters/setters/equals()/hashCode() and any usage sites (tests, services, resources) to use 'forename' consistently.
